vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: openclaw-command-center
Version: 1.4.1

The bundle provides a legitimate and well-documented command center dashboard for OpenClaw. It includes features for session monitoring, system vitals collection, and cost tracking. Security analysis shows robust practices, including path traversal protection in the static file server (src/index.js), environment variable sanitization for subprocesses (src/openclaw.js), and the use of execFile/execFileSync to mitigate shell injection risks. While the tool requires broad system access to monitor metrics and manage agents, its behavior is strictly aligned with its stated purpose, and no evidence of malicious intent, obfuscation, or unauthorized data exfiltration was found.

llm.summary: This dashboard is purpose-aligned, but its default server and authentication behavior can expose sensitive OpenClaw session data and controls beyond the local user.

dimensions.detail: The service defaults to unauthenticated mode, sets wildcard CORS, and calls `server.listen(PORT)` without applying the configured host, so sensitive dashboard APIs may be reachable outside the intended localhost-only boundary.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The install metadata is simple and transparent, running `node lib/server.js` with no remote payload retrieval or package-install hook, but it launches a long-running HTTP service.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime behavior is broader than the short SKILL.md disclosure: it starts background refresh loops, parses recent transcripts to derive operator records, persists dashboard data, and exposes additional sensitive APIs beyond the three endpoints listed in the skill text.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill writes persistent operator and privacy data under the OpenClaw profile and can modify topic status and delegate job run/pause/resume/skip/kill operations through dashboard APIs; these behaviors are related to the dashboard purpose but require tighter access control.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: A command-center dashboard reasonably needs to read sessions, usage, vitals, memory summaries, cron data, topics, and operator information, but the implementation also exposes transcript excerpts and job/topic/operator mutation endpoints while documentation claims a localhost/read-only posture that the code does not fully enforce.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are prepared to run it behind strict local or trusted-network controls. Before use, bind it explicitly to loopback, enable token or properly enforced proxy authentication, avoid exposing port 3333 to a LAN/VPN/public interface, and review whether persistent operator discovery from transcripts is acceptable for your workspace.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Verified that the artifact scans recent session transcripts for Slack, Telegram, and Discord operator identifiers and stores `operators.json`; this supports the Operators dashboard feature, but users should understand it creates persistent identity/activity metadata.
[T05] unexpected: Verified that the configured host defaults to `localhost`, but the server starts with `server.listen(PORT)` and authentication defaults to `none`, making the scanner's network exposure concern material for transcript-bearing and state-changing APIs.
[T05] unexpected: Verified that Tailscale and Cloudflare modes trust identity headers directly without validating a trusted proxy or signed Cloudflare Access token, so direct reachability can bypass the intended authentication boundary.
[T09] unexpected: Verified `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` is set on all responses, which is unnecessary for the same-origin dashboard and broadens access to sensitive APIs when auth is disabled or browser policy permits.
[T09] unexpected: Verified unescaped identity-related values are reflected in the access-denied HTML page; this is a lower-impact issue than the network/auth findings but still not expected for an auth boundary.
